messages:
cheng: Quick follow-up to the retry-state RFC — we need a clear contract for backpressure signals + midflight ownership when we do priority cutovers for streaming requests. I sketched a lightweight header and decision flow below.

sarah: Sounds important. TL;DR of the problem?

cheng: TL;DR: gateway decides to cut priority from low->high or preempt low-priority streams. We want a deterministic way for the gateway to tell the upstream runtime whether to: 1) continue producing partial stream, 2) checkpoint/resume later, or 3) abort and surface a graceful trailer. Also need a way for runtime to tell gateway if it already committed side-effects (so retries are unsafe).

aj: Do we need a new header? Can we piggyback on X-Retry-Info?

cheng: We could extend X-Retry-Info but I prefer a namespaced header so intent is explicit. Proposal: `X-RW-Stream-Ownership: <mode>=<token>;budget=<n>` where mode in {claim, release, borrow}, token is id, budget is small int for retry credits. Example: `X-RW-Stream-Ownership: claim=gw-12;budget=2`

kevin: budget semantics? is that per-request or per-client?

cheng: Per-request (moving window). Budget counts allowed midflight replays/hedges. Gateway decrements on each retry it initiates, runtime can decrement if it hedges locally. Goal: make billing + observability align with who initiated cost.

aj: What about memory/kv-cache validity when we resume? We need a checkpoint id that runtime can use to rehydrate KV. Maybe add `chkpt=` field.

cheng: Good point. Updated header: `X-RW-Stream-Ownership: claim=gw-12;budget=2;chkpt=ck-778`

kevin: If runtime responds with `X-RW-Ownership-Status: committed` then gateway should avoid retries and surface 409-ish?

cheng: Exactly. We also need a small handshake proto on first byte of streaming response so gateway can make fast decisions without waiting for end-of-stream. Example decision flow pseudocode:

```
# ingress gateway on cutover: send header with claim and budget
if upstream responds with Ownership-Status: committed:
  mark request non-retriable, send info to caller (partial/ack)
elif Ownership-Status: ok and chkpt present:
  if budget > 0:
     mark hedgable, allow one midflight resume using chkpt
  else:
     prefer graceful-abort with trailer: {error: "requeue_possible"}
```

sarah: Nice. How does this interact with cheaper hedging vs heavyweight restart? If runtime can do cheap prefix reuse we should prefer resume; otherwise abort.

cheng: Runtime should include `X-RW-Resume-Cost: cheap|expensive` on the first trailer/frame. Gateway policy: prefer resume when cheap and budget>0, abort->fallback when expensive.

aj: Observability: we need tags on traces with `rw.ownership.token` and `rw.retry.initiator` to attribute cost. Also increment a counter when gateway forces abort vs runtime aborts.

kevin: Security: tokens must be short-lived and signed so clients can't spoof. Use KMS to sign claim tokens when gateway creates them.

ops-bot: test-deploy: guideline: add e2e that simulates midflight preempt with resume vs abort, assert cost attribution metrics.

cheng: Action items: 1) I'll open an RFC PR with header names + semantics, 2) @sarah can you own trace field names, 3) @aj please add a runtime shim that emits `Ownership-Status` + `Resume-Cost` on stream start/trailer.

sarah: Ack, will pick trace keys and add dashboard tiles.

aj: Ack, will prototype shim in the runtime branch.

kevin: Minor: document how this behaves for non-streaming unary requests (should be noop besides signed token header).

cheng: Agreed — will include that. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
